title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
short: Traditional (words by Sarah Josepha Hale · C 4/4 · listen, then play it.
trouble: Reading notes one at a time instead of in chunks.

blocks.html: Your right hand stays in C position: thumb on middle C and one finger on each white key up to G. Listen for the notes that repeat. The last bar is a whole note, so hold it for all four beats.
What to notice: American nursery song, sung to the tune of “Merrily We Roll Along”

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys light up, and “wait for me” lets you practise one hand at a time.

blocks.html: Play through it once with the right hand only, then add the left. Which chord change made you stop?

sources.name: Words: Sarah Josepha Hale, Poems for Our Children (1830). Tune: the one it is usually sung to today, also used for “Merrily We Roll Along” (both from Wikipedia). Melody checked against a note-name sheet from the University of California, Riverside (gluckprogram.ucr.edu): four of its five lines match; for bar 4 that sheet uses E E E, a simpler version, and we use the usual E G G.
